```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

## Overview

`run_workflow()` chains the data, preprocessing, selection, modelling,
evaluation, and result layers into one object. The held-out validation and
test sets are transformed with parameters learned from the training set; they
are never used to fit preprocessing, selection, calibration, or thresholds.

## Build and configure the specification

```{r specification}
library(uniml)

development <- read.csv(
  system.file("extdata", "uniml-cvd-mortality.csv", package = "uniml")
)
new_admissions <- read.csv(
  system.file("extdata", "uniml-cvd-mortality-new.csv", package = "uniml")
)

spec <- uniml_spec(
  task_type = "binary",
  outcome = "died",
  positive = "yes",
  id = "id"
)
spec <- set_preprocess(
  spec,
  impute = "median_mode",
  scale = "zscore",
  encode = "onehot"
)
spec <- set_feature_selection(
  spec,
  methods = c("univariate", "lasso"),
  combine = "intersect"
)
spec <- set_learners(spec, c("lr", "cart"), tune = FALSE)
spec <- set_tuning(spec, folds = 3, evals = 5, metric = "auc")
spec <- set_evaluation(
  spec,
  ci = "bootstrap",
  threshold_method = "youden",
  calibration = "platt",
  select_on = "validation"
)
spec
```

The built-in learner keys are `lr`, `rf`, `xgb`, `lgb`, `nnet`, `knn`, `cart`,
and `nb`. Any installed mlr3 classification learner can also be passed directly,
such as `classif.log_reg`, `classif.svm`, or `classif.lda`. External learners
use their mlr3 defaults unless a custom search space is registered.

## Create leakage-safe splits

`make_split()` returns a `uniml_split` whose elements are `uniml_data`
objects. Pass the `$data` component to `run_workflow()`. The independent
new-admission cohort stays outside the development split.

```{r split}
split <- make_split(
  as_uniml_data(development, spec),
  prop = c(0.8, 0.2),
  stratify = TRUE,
  seed = 123
)

names(split)
nrow(split$train$data)
nrow(split$validation$data)
nrow(new_admissions)
```

## Run the workflow

```{r workflow}
result <- run_workflow(
  spec,
  train = split$train$data,
  validation = split$validation$data,
  test = new_admissions,
  ci_R = 200
)

result
summary(result)
```

The result stores the fitted preprocessor, selection details, tuning
records, cross-validation output, metrics with confidence intervals,
predictions, thresholds, and the model ranking. Useful components include:

```{r inspect-results}
result$metrics
result$ci
result$ranking
result$models
result$selection$selected_features
```

The comparison set is controlled by `set_evaluation(select_on = ...)` and
`rank_models(select_on = ...)`. With `"auto"`, the test set is used when
available; otherwise validation is used. For external validation, set
`select_on = "validation"` so model selection is not optimised on the new
admission cohort.

## Predict new data

`predict_uniml()` reuses the stored preprocessing, selected feature mapping,
calibration, threshold, and fitted learner. It does not refit anything.

```{r predict}
predicted <- predict_uniml(
  result,
  newdata = new_admissions,
  model = "best"
)
head(predicted)
```

The `newdata` argument may omit the outcome column. In that case the returned
data frame contains predicted probabilities and classes without a truth
column.

## Leakage policies

The default is a transparent custom policy. It can be changed explicitly:

```{r leakage}
spec_in <- set_leakage_policy(
  spec,
  mode = "strict_in",
  in_cv = c("selection", "balance", "tuning")
)

spec_out <- set_leakage_policy(spec, mode = "strict_out")
```

`strict_in` repeats configured steps inside each cross-validation fold.
`strict_out` keeps those steps outside the fold loop. The validation and test
sets remain held out in both cases.

## Export results

After inspecting the result, data tables and figures can be written with
`export_results()`. The workflow result is also the input to the
performance and SHAP plotting functions.
